Responding Spatial Count Patterns and Their Persistence

Updated October 18, 2026

This calculation retains its stated assumptions and action. For the current ten-space-plus-time physical picture, common-frequency portions and later developments, see the new particle-geometry and sector-depths case.

Current interpretation. This article preserves an 18 October inverse construction. Its supplied count-valued spectral clocks and separately excited response modes are mathematical comparison models. They are not a realization of the current proposal of C portions sharing one fundamental frequency, whose additive average registration rate is C times that fundamental. Persistence and response conclusions below apply only to the action and domains actually written here; they do not transfer to a different action. The current particle-geometry account develops that distinction and the newer constructions.

An explicit conservative action can join a count clock, four independently changing spatial profiles, responding anisotropic support and a full spatial response of the same field. Its isolated circular families have a nonlinear persistence basin at fixed total phase charge, including the response contribution. Two patterns in this same action exchange charge and exert actual spatial forces. A controlled finite encounter theorem survives, while an exact coincident-source solution shows why positive energy and total charge alone do not ensure that each retained displacement remains nonzero forever.

Two related phase-neutral actions instead conserve each pattern's phase charge. One adds a positive direct overlap term and is repulsive where overlap decreases with separation. The other uses a common saturated source and has an attractive static cross contribution. Each has a precise sufficient two-core persistence budget. They change the temporal phase behavior as well as the force law.

This advances the previous persistence and response construction, which established spatial persistence and responding modes in separate actions. Here the spatial profiles, supporting geometry and response are varied in one action before proving its energy identity. The fixed-template pair calculations supply useful spectral comparisons, but their kinetic alternatives and coefficients are not silently transferred to this action.

All spatial directions are ordinary directions of one shared physical space, taken here as R10\mathbb R^{10}R10, without compactification. Components and coefficients describe Ψ∞\Psi_\inftyΨ∞​; they are not additional spatial dimensions, mediator particles or position probabilities. The internal classical fields below remain distinct from the electron's literal external trajectory in its surrounding six-dimensional space. A finite normal envelope is an input to these examples, not a derivation of exact layer confinement.

Reproducibility and remaining physical inputs

The accepted original calculations contain 1,567 checks for the signed-source construction and 366 for the density-source construction. A separate 530-check comparison rederived the shared identities, exact transfer and boundary velocity, both neutral completions, all fourteen clock rows, 91 diagnostic detunings and 105 spatial overlaps. A further independently implemented 152-check backcheck verified the new transfer, cap and neutral-budget results. Each was replayed unchanged; these are separate executed scopes, not a sum of independent physical confirmations. No full nonlinear encounter time integration or observed lifetime was computed.

A new standalone scoped checker and its results verify selected displayed identities with exact rational arithmetic, check the exact invariant oscillator solution and nonzero boundary velocity numerically, and check the fourteen count labels. It uses only Python's standard library and no private research inputs. It does not rerun the original 1,567, 366, 530 or 152 checks, the 105 spatial quadratures, or a nonlinear persistence simulation. The provenance record identifies its exact executed bytes and distinguishes the original evidence scopes.

The supplied clock units and occupied labels, finite band, normalized source representation, four-profile/common-phase restriction, material connection, support and variance laws, inverse compensation and collective center inertia remain inverse inputs. The new neutral laws additionally supply either a direct cross term or a saturation scale. The results establish useful same-action stationarity, finite-band persistence, full-response accounting and conditional pair mechanisms. Physical boost inertia, fundamental field content, layer confinement, electric charge, spin, measured coupling strengths and observed persistence still require derivation. No photon identification, completed mass operator or empirical preference for particular depths is claimed.
